P1.evidence: 'I already saw your application, but I would just like to hear everything from you' — read but not read back, so nothing was reflected. Three-part frame again, missing 'what's in the way' and 'what you need'. Agreement obtained ('Sounds good?' — 'All right. Sounds good.') and the open question ran.

P2.evidence: Age and weight were both volunteered, never asked — 'I'm 71' and 'I'm at 179' came out of the prospect's own goal narrative, which the script scores as a miss. Height never established. Occupation never asked: that he runs businesses, works with people in India and is buying property in Hawaii all surfaced incidentally. No health-conditions question. Injuries asked properly and productively — 'Do you have any aches, pains that come up for you?' — which produced the annual water-skiing injuries and the chiropractor history. Current training asked ('What are you actually doing with workouts at the moment?'). Diet interrogated well, down to his macro split and whether he eats out. Sleep and energy never asked.

P3.evidence: The surface goal was pinned down well — 'when it comes to getting your best shape possible, what does that look like for Kevin?' produced target weights and a physique reference. The why was asked directly ('I'm so curious why. Why?') and answered with 'I want to live to 150.' Then it stopped. The rep never asked what living to 150 in good shape would actually do for him, never asked who else it impacts, and never drove through to family, legacy or identity — a 71-year-old man with businesses, adventures and a Hawaii property plan and not one question about who any of it is for. The reflect-back was a light summary ('it sounds like you want to optimize more') rather than the scripted 'this isn't really about X, it's about Y'.

P4.evidence: The phase did not run at all. Thirteen years of training history, a 49-pound weight loss, a gym he has stopped attending and a stale morning routine were all mentioned and none of it was explored. No 'what have you tried', no 'what happened with that', no 'why didn't it stick', and the prospect was never given the chance to name a structural gap. Applicable throughout and simply not done.

P5.evidence: The rep did open the door — 'why now? Why not just wait a couple of more months with changing it up?' — and got a straight admission that there was no urgency: 'I could wait a couple more months, I mean, I've got plenty of other things I can do... I've got no real answer to that.' That is the moment the consequence frame exists for. The rep replied 'it sounds like it's just a thing that you want to change, want to go for it' and moved on. No two-year picture, no settle question, no 'why not', no line in the sand.

P6.evidence: No commitment check of any kind before presenting. Neither the belief question nor the 'any reason you wouldn't go all in' question was asked, and both prices were on the table with no verbal yes behind them. The prospect had already told the rep at 00:11:58 that he had no reason to act now, and the script's instruction is to return to Phase 5 on exactly that hesitation.

P11.evidence: Both offers were deferred to the following day, so payment and onboarding were never reachable. No link sent, no Trevor call booked, no agreement.

objection_plays.detail: 'Let me give it some thought. I'm not prepared to take either one of them today.' One OA move ran, and ran late — at 00:19:44, two minutes after the deferral had already been accepted and logistics arranged: 'I'm just curious if you want to give it a thought for yourself, but what would stop you from saying, let's go right now?' That surfaced the real blocker. Nothing else ran: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no identity close, no 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in?'

'Just financially, I just got to take a look at where I can put it.' The rep ran exactly one move — breaking it up — and ran it unprompted and immediately: 'if you feel like, well, 1,000 upfront is too much, just let me know and we can also split it up into six times or two or whatever.' No isolation question, and not one of the six financial-picture questions: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments. On a prospect who had just described buying property in Hawaii, the financial picture was the single most valuable thing available and it was never asked for.

SCRIPT GAP — 'I just want the plan, not the coaching.' At 00:13:03 the prospect disqualified himself from the $6,000 product before it had ever been described: 'I don't necessarily need to work one-on-one.' There is no scripted play for a prospect who self-selects down to the cheapest tier, so the rep accepted it, led with the $1,000 option and presented the $6,000 one only when asked. The core offer was never actually sold on this call.

SCRIPT GAP — clinical fit for an older prospect with a recurring injury. The prospect disclosed annual water-skiing back injuries and near-annual chiropractic treatment at 00:08:09. The script has no screen for this, and the rep's improvisation ran the wrong way: he described the self-serve tier as 'made to those that don't have massive injuries' and then recommended that unsupervised tier to a 71-year-old with a recurring back problem.

notes: Four of the seven phases effectively did not run. P4, P5 and P6 are outright misses, and the rep had the opening handed to him — the prospect said in plain terms that he had no reason to act now, and that admission was accepted rather than worked. Price landed sixteen minutes into a twenty-three minute call with no consequence and no commitment behind it, and three of the remaining minutes went on banter about the rep's age. Coach: when a prospect says 'I've got no real answer to that', go to Phase 5, do not move on.
